prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1469; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened after the insured's vehicle was sideswiped while changing lanes. The claimant reports a knee injury from the impact and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that the policy was active at the time of loss. Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates coverage.

Entry 3: Police report and two independent witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the collision. Photos from the scene are consistent with the description given.

Entry 4: Spoke with the other driver, who confirms the accident happened as the claimant described, with the other vehicle drifting into the claimant's lane during a lane change.

Entry 5: Claimant gave the same account of the accident in each conversation so far, including sequence of events and point of impact.

Entry 6: Reviewed the knee injury report. The injury is plausible for a side impact of this type. No prior injury to the same area is known from the claimant's history or available records.

Entry 7: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this injury. Requested updated treatment notes and a breakdown of visits to better understand the timeline.

Entry 8: Vehicle inspection completed. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known from the prior claims search or the inspection itself.

Entry 9: Estimator notes that some of the body damage may not be from this impact. It is not yet clear whether all of the listed repairs relate to this loss, so the estimate is on hold for further review.

Entry 10: Referred the open items on the injury treatment timeline and the separation of damage to the reviewing supervisor. Claim remains open pending those responses.
